meaning: to face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage and accept it
literal_translation: encarar uma situação difícil com coragem, mesmo sem vontade
example: I hate going to the dentist, but I'll have to bite the bullet and book the appointment.
origin: Possibly from the time before anesthesia, when patients were said to bite on a bullet during painful procedures; this origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to eat a quick snack during a busy work day
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with food or eating; it describes facing a difficulty.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse a request firmly and politely
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom means accepting something hard, not refusing it.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to damage a metal object by hitting it
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a literal and unrelated image; the idiom has no meaning of physical damage.

explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to accept a painful or difficult situation bravely, usually because there is no way to avoid it. It is common in everyday and professional English.
